fixes.explanation: I get the guess, friend, because this chapter is crawling with priests. But the verse names something else: Christ is mediator so that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance. The verse says nothing about handing out priest jobs.

A long life sounds lovely, and I would take extra years in my bakery any day. But Hebrews 9:15 says those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance. Eternal, baker. That's a different size of gift than a few good decades.

Yes, baker. Christ died to redeem them from the transgressions committed under the first covenant (Hebrews 9:15). So His death reaches the transgressions from the first covenant. First is the word that fits.

Good eye, friend, because that word is in the verse. It just belongs to another spot: the promised eternal inheritance. The transgressions in question were committed under the first covenant (Hebrews 9:15). Right word, other oven.

Everyone agreeing is a nice thought, friend. But Hebrews 9:17 says a will does not take effect until the one who made it has died. The writer never mentions anyone agreeing. It all hangs on that death.
Fields and flocks are a fair guess, friend. But the text says Moses sprinkled the scroll and all the people (Hebrews 9:19). No mention of the fields, and no mention of a single sheep.

Yes, baker. In the same way, Moses sprinkled with blood the tabernacle and all the vessels used in worship (Hebrews 9:21). The scroll and the people were sprinkled first (Hebrews 9:19). Now the tabernacle and the vessels are covered too.

Gates and walls sound like a big job, but they're not in the verse. Hebrews 9:21 says he sprinkled with blood the tabernacle and all the vessels used in worship. It's about the tabernacle and what was used in worship.
That would take a long afternoon, friend, and the writer doesn't say it. Hebrews 9:21 says Moses sprinkled the tabernacle and all the vessels used in worship. The tribes' own tents never come up.

Smaller is a fair guess, friend, but the verse goes another way. It says the heavenly things themselves needed better sacrifices than these (Hebrews 9:23). It's about quality, and the text doesn't say a word about size.

Older doesn't fit, baker. The verse says it was necessary for the heavenly things themselves to be purified with better sacrifices than these (Hebrews 9:23). The writer is comparing the copies with the real thing, and he calls the sacrifices better.

Right, baker. Hebrews 9:25 says Christ did not enter heaven to offer Himself again and again. The high priest enters the Most Holy Place every year with blood that is not his own. Christ's offering is not a yearly one like that.
Prayers are a good thing, friend, but that's not the word here. The verse says Christ “…was offered once to bear the sins of many…” (Hebrews 9:28). Sins is the word the writer uses.
Moses and the law get a lot of space in this passage, baker. But the verse says He will bring salvation to those who eagerly await Him (Hebrews 9:28). Those who kept the law aren't named there.
